title: Solve self-consistent mean-field TIM for layered system
action: Implement the mean-field Transverse Ising Model for a quasi-2D layered ferroelectric with exponentially graded interlayer coupling K_nm ∝ exp(−λ|n−m|). Write a numerical solver (e.g., fixed-point iteration or root-finding) to obtain self-consistent layer-resolved pseudospin averages ⟨S_n^z⟩ as a function of system size N, grading parameter λ, normalized temperature kBT/K, and reduced applied field e_z/K. Store the resulting layer-resolved polarization array for all parameter combinations.
description: Intermediate layer polarization array used as building block for macroscopic dielectric responses.
output_schema: Array of shape (num_field_points, N) containing layer-resolved ⟨S_n^z⟩ for each reduced electric field.

title: Compute and output macroscopic dielectric and tunability responses
action: From the solved layer-resolved pseudospin averages, calculate: (1) mean polarization ⟨P^z⟩ as the average over layers, (2) dielectric susceptibility χ from the numerical derivative of ⟨P^z⟩ with respect to e_z (using adjacent field points), and (3) tunability percentage η = (χ(0)−χ(E))/χ(0) × 100. Generate a single CSV file containing the results for parameter sets (N=5, λ=0.0), (N=5, λ=0.261), (N=50, λ=0.0), (N=50, λ=0.01) at reduced temperature kBT/K=1.0 and reduced field e_z/K from 0 to 2 in steps of 0.1.
description: CSV with computed mean polarization, dielectric susceptibility, and tunability for all field and parameter combinations. All quantities dimensionless (polarization reduced, susceptibility dimensionless, tunability in percent 0-100).
output_schema: Header: N, lambda, kBT_K, e_z_over_K, mean_polarization, dielectric_susceptibility, tunability_percentage. Each row corresponds to one (N, lambda, e_z_over_K) combination at fixed kBT_K=1.0. All fields numeric.
